planning_notes: Preserve all supplied wiring. No source component IDs were supplied, so device identifiers are omitted.
D2 uses the disclosed GND-switch semantics: INPUT_PULLUP and active LOW. Its normalized model input is true when active; do not invert it again.
Keep ADC inputs raw and perform the disclosed current and LM35 calibrations in the SysML model using floating-point arithmetic and the 5 V ADC reference.

Compute status on every control step: 3 for active vibration, otherwise 2 for temperature > 60 C, otherwise 1 for current > 7 A, otherwise 0. Recompute on release as well as activation; faults are not latched.
Control the fan independently of status priority: PWM 255 whenever temperature > 60 C, and 0 otherwise, including during mechanical faults.
Alarm cadence and frequency are unspecified. Assume a continuous 1000 Hz tone and steady illuminated LED during mechanical faults, both off otherwise.

Serial fault-message text and repetition cadence are unspecified. Assume an unprefixed integer line containing 3 on every mechanical-fault entry, not only the first entry. No normal-state reporting or serial receiver is required.

Rotate current, temperature, and status pages every 2000 ms using actual elapsed deltas. Assume current is the initial page and truncate nonnegative measurements to integers for display only; threshold comparisons use unrounded measurements.
Refresh the selected display page from current model values each step without resetting page timing when inputs change. Do not retain a stale fault status after vibration clears.

Initialize outputs off and display command zero, then evaluate available inputs immediately. Meet the 250 ms reaction bound and return from setup within 500 ms without blocking display or alarm delays.

interfaces.name: io_0
interfaces.meaning: Motor current sensor raw ADC reading; model converts to amperes using ADC * 10 / 1023.

interfaces.name: io_1
interfaces.meaning: LM35 raw ADC reading with 5 V ADC reference; model converts to Celsius using ADC * 500 / 1023.

interfaces.name: io_2
interfaces.meaning: Vibration switch active; normalized true when the switch connects D2 to GND.

interfaces.name: io_3
interfaces.meaning: Cooling fan PWM command in counts from 0 to 255.

interfaces.name: io_4
interfaces.meaning: Mechanical-fault audible alarm frequency in Hz; zero silences the buzzer.

interfaces.name: io_6
interfaces.meaning: Whole integer selected by the model from current in amperes, temperature in Celsius, or status code.

interfaces.name: io_7
interfaces.meaning: Actual elapsed milliseconds since the previous control step, with first delta zero, for display page timing.

interfaces.name: serial_0_trigger
interfaces.meaning: Report once on each entry into mechanical-fault status, including a fault active at the first evaluated step.

interfaces.name: serial_0_value_0
interfaces.meaning: Mechanical fault code; the model supplies 3 whenever the report is triggered.

Operational acceptance profile operational-acceptance-v4 (additional public experimental conditions, not raw dataset text):
- Explicit original requirements and supplied circuit connections override every default below.
- Where no electrical wiring is supplied, individual LEDs are active HIGH to GND and buttons connect the named input to GND with INPUT_PULLUP; model pressed values are normalized independently of electrical level.
- When unspecified, a counter starts at zero and an LED starts OFF. An explicitly required ON state takes precedence.
- When the original gives no reaction deadline, a digital/button/serial command, PWM duty command or servo ANGLE COMMAND must update within 250ms of its input event becoming available. This does not impose physical motor travel time, shorten an explicit delay, or change a specified sensor/report period.
- When the original gives no display refresh period or response deadline, a changed input must be reflected in the display within 250ms. Explicit original display periods, delays and startup sequences override this default. This additional display bound was explicitly authorized for this experimental variant.
- Where the requirement asks to continuously stream a Boolean button/switch state over Serial but gives no repeat interval, respond to a changed state within 250ms and emit its correct state message at least once in every 500ms stable-state interval after settling. Explicit original report periods and event-only reporting rules override this default. This authorized additional continuous-state-report condition does not apply to startup-only messages, command echoes, sensor sampling or persistent display contents. A display retaining the correct visible state requires no repeated print calls unless the source explicitly requires redraws.
- Unless the original specifies a warmup or delayed startup, setup() must return within 500ms. Deadlines stated after initialization are measured from the observed setup() return, not power-on.
- An unspecified continuous DHT report must eventually emit a fresh valid reading within 3000ms of that measurement becoming available; explicit reporting periods override this bound.

requirement_checks.reason: All functional clauses are consistent with the implementation as detailed in the R1 check. The contract preserves A0 current acquisition, A1 LM35 acquisition, D2 vibration, D5 fan PWM, D6 tone, D13 LED and Serial. Its TM1637 binding uses the authoritative resolved CLK D4 and DIO D3 assignment, superseding the original DIO D5 assignment. D2 uses INPUT_PULLUP with LOW normalized to true; the model consumes that Boolean without another inversion. The LED is active HIGH and initially OFF. Timer and edge-history states start at zero/false. The serial configuration specifies 9600 baud, line_or_idle framing and a 20 ms idle timeout; the registered adapter initializes at 9600 baud. Five-millisecond sampling and control scheduling, with no model-imposed reaction delay, are consistent with the 250 ms command-response bound. Selected display values refresh each step while page selection follows the explicit two-second period. Neither model nor contract prescribes startup blocking that contradicts the 500 ms setup bound. Continuous Boolean streaming and DHT-specific defaults are inapplicable. These findings establish model-boundary consistency, not measured execution timing.

requirement_checks.requirement_quote: Status0 normal,1 overload, 2 overheat,3 mechanical fault; mechanical fault has highest priority, then overheat.
requirement_checks.reason: Registered analog acquisition supplies raw 0–1023 ADC counts with unit scale and zero offset, so the real-valued formulas implement both required calibrations without double scaling or integer division. Status uses strict, unrounded current >7 A and temperature >60 C comparisons, prioritizing mechanical fault, then overheat, then overload. ADC current values 716/717 and temperature values 122/123 fall on opposite sides of their respective thresholds. Status is recomputed on release rather than latched. Fan output io_3 independently selects 255 above 60 C and zero otherwise; the registered PWM mapping preserves those electrical commands even during mechanical faults. Active vibration commands io_4=1000 Hz and io_5=true, with zero/false on release. The ordered faultEntry update captures io_2 AND NOT previousVibration before updating previousVibration. Consequently an initially active first sample and each later activation produce a one-step report gate; held faults do not repeat. The serial value is 3 whenever that gate is true, and the registered empty label yields an unprefixed numeric line. No alternative alarm frequency or report repetition interval is required. The display timer adds actual elapsed milliseconds through io_7 and then reduces modulo 6000 before outputs are evaluated. Output io_6 selects floored current below 2000 ms, floored temperature below 4000 ms, and current status otherwise. This preserves residual elapsed time, handles multicycle deltas, refreshes the selected measurement without resetting rotation, and starts on current because the first delta is zero. Flooring is consistent with integer display of these nonnegative measurements. All requested interfaces are present; the explicitly authorized DIO remapping to D3 supersedes R1's original D5 display wiring.

limitations: This is a model-boundary consistency review, not runtime success or final code acceptance. Model-authored test descriptions were not treated as executed evidence.

requirement_checks.requirement_quote: Status0 normal,1 overload, 2 overheat,3 mechanical fault; mechanical fault has highest priority, then overheat.
requirement_checks.reason: Registered analog acquisition supplies raw 0–1023 ADC counts with unit scale and zero offset, so the real-valued formulas implement both required calibrations without double scaling or integer division. Status uses strict, unrounded current >7 A and temperature >60 C comparisons, prioritizing mechanical fault, then overheat, then overload. ADC current values 716/717 and temperature values 122/123 fall on opposite sides of their respective thresholds. Status is recomputed on release rather than latched. Fan output io_3 independently selects 255 above 60 C and zero otherwise; the registered PWM mapping preserves those electrical commands even during mechanical faults. Active vibration commands io_4=1000 Hz and io_5=true, with zero/false on release. The ordered faultEntry update captures io_2 AND NOT previousVibration before updating previousVibration. Consequently an initially active first sample and each later activation produce a one-step report gate; held faults do not repeat. The serial value is 3 whenever that gate is true, and the registered empty label yields an unprefixed numeric line. No alternative alarm frequency or report repetition interval is required. The display timer adds actual elapsed milliseconds through io_7 and then reduces modulo 6000 before outputs are evaluated. Output io_6 selects floored current below 2000 ms, floored temperature below 4000 ms, and current status otherwise. This preserves residual elapsed time, handles multicycle deltas, refreshes the selected measurement without resetting rotation, and starts on current because the first delta is zero. Flooring is consistent with integer display of these nonnegative measurements. All requested interfaces are present; the explicitly authorized DIO remapping to D3 supersedes R1's original D5 display wiring.
